content:
- Model consistently underestimates true price spikes, especially in the first 10–15 days of the 30d horizon; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for early spikes.
- Model overestimates mean price in the middle of the horizon; reduce forecast slope slightly after day 10–12 to avoid over-optimism.
- After a sharp spike in true outcome (e.g., >85), model tends to overshoot and continue rising; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use mean-reversion anchor.
- Sentiment history is always 0.00 — no sentiment signal — so ignore sentiment-based adjustments; rely solely on price pattern and lagged behavior.
- Model exhibits strong lag: true price often peaks 2–4 days before model forecast peaks; shift forecast forward by 2–3 days for better alignment.
- In cases where true outcome shows sharp downward correction after spike, model fails to adjust; add a 1–2 day “cool-down” buffer before resuming upward trend.
